meta.purpose: Single source of truth for game content. The engine implements the small vocabularies below (traits, effects, statuses) once; new content should reuse them. If an entry needs a new verb, add it to the vocabulary first.

status_meanings.phase2: Needs the camp or the server (Phase 2). Keep it in the file, don't spawn it yet.
status_meanings.later: Designed and held for a later content batch.
status_meanings.concept: Idea only. Needs design before use.

meta.never_delete: Mark retired content "status": "retired" instead of deleting it, so old floors and runs still load and replay.
meta.text_rules: "text" is hand-written flavor, 120 characters max, in the voice of docs/WRITING.md. Rules text ("HP 4 · Hits 1d3 · Fast") is generated from the stats at display time, never hand-written, so it can't go stale.

rules.movement: 8-directional, for the player and monsters alike, with no corner cutting: a diagonal step is blocked when either tile it passes beside is a wall; a diagonal attack (or disarm) out of a 1-wide doorway needs only one of them open. Tap a tile to walk there by the shortest path; stop early whenever something new comes into view. D-pad remains as an option.
rules.turns: Player acts, then monsters, using ROT.Scheduler.Speed. Speeds: slow = 50 (acts every other turn), normal = 100, fast = 200 (acts twice per player turn).
rules.damage: roll(attacker's weapon or natural dice) - roll(0 to defender.armor), the armor rolled fresh on every hit, minimum 1 on a hit.
rules.natural_regen: None. Walking and waiting heal nothing. HP comes back from health potions, bandages, food and a worn item's regen. Monsters don't regenerate.
rules.hp_between_floors: HP and ailments carry down the stairs, with no rest heal (decided 2026-10-13). After a death the next floor starts at full HP with no ailments. Phase 2: the camp is where you heal.
rules.holding_ground: When one side steps into the other's reach (beside it, any of the 8 neighbors), the one already there gets the edge: if its next action is an attack on the newcomer, the hit roll is made twice and the better one counts. Only hunting monsters get it. An equal-speed chaser still can't hit someone who keeps moving away.
rules.field_of_view: ROT.FOV.PreciseShadowcasting with the creature's sight radius. The player sees a tile in that line of sight only while it's lit (rules.lighting). Tiles once seen stay drawn but dimmed (explored). Monsters notice the player by line of sight alone; light doesn't hide anyone yet.

lighting.always_lit: The start room and the guardian's room, each with a torch over the player's or guardian's column.

monster_states.asleep: Doesn't move. Each turn the player is within 2 tiles, 50% chance to wake. Always wakes when hit or alarmed.
monster_states.wander: Random walk. Starts hunting when it has line of sight to the player within its sight radius.
monster_states.hunting: Chases by A* path. After 8 turns without seeing the player, goes back to wandering.
monster_states.hidden: Ambusher. Doesn't move or show until the player comes within its sight radius, then hunts.

traps.detection: At the start of each player turn, every hidden trap within 1 tile is revealed with chance = search% + the trap's detect_mod. The lantern reveals adjacent traps automatically.
traps.disarm: Beside a known, armed trap, disarming takes a turn and works with chance = search% + 30 + the trap's detect_mod. A success earns 2 XP. The omen doesn't change it. A failure sets the trap off on you, as if you'd stepped on it.
traps.monsters: Monsters never trigger traps. They live here.
traps.ghost_reveal: Traps your partner triggered or detected on this floor are revealed for you (Milestone 4).

floor_budget.monsters: 7 + floor(floor number / 2), max 13. A group counts as its members.
floor_budget.special_rooms: 0 to 2, rolled from the rooms list.
floor_budget.exit: The stairs down, placed in the farthest third of the floor by path distance from the start. Since content 36 (exit_in_the_open) only on a tile with floor on all 8 sides, so the stairs have a buffer of floor around them; nothing is placed on those 9 tiles, and no rug, cover or tile look lies there, only the room's floor.

loot.per_player: Layout, monsters and traps come from the shared floor seed. Item rolls (chest contents, drops) use the floor seed plus the player's slot (A or B), so the two of you find different things in the same places. This is what makes trading worth doing.
loot.deck: A chest's item is drawn when it's opened, from a deck the character carries, one per rarity: an item doesn't come up again until every other item of its rarity has. The kit's starting gear starts drawn. A monster's rarity drop draws from the same deck. A death starts a new deck.
loot.pity: After 4 chests in a row that gave commons, the next one gives uncommon or better.
loot.stash: Content 16. Cover with 'hides' (straw) hides a stash in a patch with its chance: one tile of the patch, shared by both players, holding a gold pile's worth rolled per player. Stepping onto it finds it and picks it up in the same move. When the cover burns out, the gold is left in the open.

death.phase1: The floor ends and the run is recorded.
death.phase2: You wake at camp with half HP and lose the gold you found that day.
death.retry: In practice and checks, a death offers Continue?: the same floor again from its start. You come back in your gear, with the level, XP and HP you came down with, but at least 1/3 of your max HP (rounded up). Your grave sack lies where you fell: it holds the items and gold the floor gave you, and keeps 95% of the XP you earned there (rounded down). Die again before you reach it and it's gone. Monsters come back; one you killed gives no XP or drops again. The daily floor keeps one attempt.

art.motion_format: art.motion names how a kit or monster moves a tile (one of art.motions); without one it slides plainly. Lengths are map pixels (a tile is 8), times are ms. ms: the travel. ease: linear, in, out or in_out. hop: arc height, hops: arcs per tile. steps: travel in that many jerks (0 = smooth). tilt: degrees it rocks. stretch: how much it stretches along the way. land_ms and land_squash: a squash on landing, after the travel. ms + land_ms stays under 200 (tap-walk's step).

stomp.text: Heavy and sure: lifts a little, lands hard.

flutter.text: Bobs up and down the whole way.

scamper.text: Hunched and shifty, rocking side to side.

ooze.text: Stretches toward where it's going, then catches up.

lurch.text: A wooden bound, then a thump.

trudge.text: Too heavy to hurry, swaying as it comes.

style_rules: 8x8, opaque, ink background. Ink inside the sprite works as outline and negative space.
At most 5 non-ink colors per sprite.
Creatures face the viewer, roughly symmetric, filling about 6x6 to 8x8.
Weapons and wands point diagonally from bottom-left to top-right.
Potions and vials are upright and centered, cork or neck on top.
Readable at 1x: within one biome, no two enemies share both silhouette and main color.
Never rely on color alone to tell two things apart. Shape must differ too (accessibility).
art.generator_prompt_template: {size}x{size} pixel art roguelike {kind} sprite: {silhouette}. Key features: {features}. Colors: {colors}. {pose}. Opaque background {ink_hex}. Hard pixels, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering. Use only this palette: {palette_hex_list}.
art.set_piece_prompt_template: {width}x{height} pixel art scene: {scene}. Mood: {mood}. Same palette as the game ({palette_hex_list}), ink background, hard pixels, no anti-aliasing. Characters drawn as in their 8x8 sprites but larger: {characters}.

set_pieces_planned.scene: two travelers at a campfire in a cave mouth, packs set down, embers rising
the Rat King on a heap of barrels, crown askew
one frame per story beat, defined with the story skeleton

erratic.does: Each move, with this chance, steps to a random open adjacent tile instead of toward its target.

steal_gold.does: On a hit, takes this much gold instead of dealing damage, then flees toward the exit and leaves the floor if it gets there. Drops everything it stole when killed.

on_hit_status.does: When its attack hits, applies the status with this chance.

ranged_status.does: If the player is in line of sight within range and the cooldown is ready, spends its turn applying the status at range instead of moving.

disguised.does: Drawn exactly as the prop and doesn't act until the player bumps, opens or attacks it. Then it reveals itself and gets a free attack.

reassemble.does: On death leaves a bone_pile that rises again with full HP after the delay, up to 'times', unless the killing blow came from a weapon with unless_tag.

split_on_hit.does: When hit and it survives with at least min_hp left, splits into two copies, each with half its remaining HP (rounded down) and half its XP.

death_cloud.does: On death, fills tiles within radius with a cloud for 'turns' turns. Anything standing in it gets the status.

heals_allies.does: When off cooldown, heals the most-hurt ally in range instead of attacking.

flees_when_adjacent.does: Steps away when the player is adjacent, if it can.

hunts_by_sound.does: Ignores sight. Moves toward the most recent noise within hearing range (combat, traps, breaking things). A player who waits in place makes no noise.

summons.does: Every 'every' turns, spawns one 'enemy' adjacent to itself, up to max_alive at once.

shared_hp.does: Guardian. One HP pool shared by both players across days. Damage either of you deals is saved when your run ends; the guardian floor repeats daily until the pool hits 0. Until Phase 2, each player fights a normal copy.

reach.does: Weapon. Can attack an enemy up to 'range' tiles away in a straight line with nothing in between.

ranged.does: Weapon or wand. Attacks a visible enemy within range. Adjacent attacks use the melee numbers instead.

stun_on_hit.does: Weapon. Hits apply 'stunned' with this chance.

charges.does: Limited uses. One comes back every 'every' turns until it's full; the recharge rule says the rest.

params.turns: n (optional: the status's default_turns, which may be "rest of floor")

params.ignites: true to light the flammable cover in the area (optional)

params.dmg: dice, or a whole number for a flat amount

statuses.label: Rooted
statuses.text: Stuck fast. You can still swing.

statuses.label: Burning
statuses.text: On fire. It's as bad as it sounds.

statuses.label: Fed
statuses.text: Something in your stomach. The ache eases, slowly.

statuses.label: Hidden
statuses.text: They can't see you. Don't push it.

statuses.label: Soaked
statuses.text: Wet to the knees. Slower to dodge, and very hard to set alight.

statuses.label: Blessed
statuses.text: Something old is on your side tonight.

statuses.label: Pressing On
statuses.text: You walked past the fire. The next chest had better be worth it.

kits.name: Warden
kits.role: Front line. Takes hits and holds corridors.
kits.text: Sword, leather, two health potions. Stands in the corridor so nothing gets past.

kits.name: Lamplighter
kits.role: Scout. Sees further, spots traps, fights at range.
kits.text: Bow, cloak, lantern. Sees it coming, and sees what's underfoot.

biomes.name: The Cellars
biomes.text: The old lords' storerooms, full of barrels, bones and rats, with coal dust ground into every stone.

guardian.layout: One great hall with two side rooms.
guardian.exit_rules: Phase 1: the ladder down is there from the start; the guardian is optional, for its loot. Phase 2: a ladder back up is always available (retreat to camp, damage is banked), and the ladder down appears only when the shared HP pool hits 0.

biomes.name: The Fungal Hollows
biomes.text: The old coal workings dumped their spoil here. It's still warm, so the fungus has never stopped growing.

guardian.layout: A round cavern ringed with spore pods.

biomes.name: The Drowned Halls
biomes.text: These halls are older than the old lords, and flooded when their shafts broke through. The water isn't empty.

generator.extra: Add shallow water pools from the sheet's water tiles (columns 11-13, rows 6-8). Water ends burning.

biomes.design_notes: Ideas: eels that only attack from water tiles, drowned sailors, crabs (sheet tile [12, 0]), an imp (tile [11, 1]) or the eye creature (tile [13, 0]) as the guardian.

enemies.name: Cellar Rat
enemies.text: Fat on whatever fell down here before you. Never alone.

tidbits.text: The rats came for the old lords' grain. It ran out centuries ago, so now they eat whatever they can catch.
Rat pelts used to sell for a copper a dozen. I've stopped buying them. Nobody in town is that cold yet.
Rats in town are no bigger than a fist. The big ones come up only as far as the cellars, which is rather fortunate.

art.silhouette: small four-legged rodent, low and wide

enemies.name: Cave Bat
enemies.text: It never flies straight, so don't bother aiming where it was.

tidbits.text: Bats roost up in the old shafts and come down into the cellars to hunt. Something keeps those shafts warm.
The alchemist buys bat droppings by the jar. She won't say what for, and nobody has pressed her.
The bats used to keep to the deep shafts. These days they come up a little higher every winter.

art.silhouette: bat with wings spread wide

enemies.name: Skeleton
enemies.text: One of the old lords' diggers, still in his work belt. He was sent down, and only a crushing blow keeps him down.

tidbits.text: The skeletons wear the old lords' work belts and tool loops. Some of them still have the tools.
We bury them in pieces now. It's more work, but they stay where we put them.
Skeletons turn up only in the old lords' workings. The older halls below don't have a single bone.

art.silhouette: standing human skeleton, arms at sides

enemies.name: Goblin Cutpurse
enemies.text: Doesn't want a fight. Wants your purse, then the nearest exit.

tidbits.text: Goblins steal coins, never gear. Nobody has any idea what they do with them.
Goblins can write, a little. They keep a tally of every purse they've taken, scratched into the walls.
Goblin gold is always old lords' coin. I'd love to know where they find it. I don't ask, of course.

art.silhouette: small hunched humanoid with a big sack

enemies.name: Web Spinner
enemies.text: Waits in the dark corners. The web comes first, then the bite.

tidbits.text: Web spinners string their webs across doorways at head height, where a tall person walks straight in.
Spider silk makes the best thread there is. Don't ask where my stitches come from.
Some webs down here are so old they've gone grey with dust. Whatever spun them is still around.

art.silhouette: round-bodied spider, eight legs splayed
features: legs reaching to the tile edges

enemies.name: Cellar Adder
enemies.text: Lies still where the straw is deepest. Most people find it with an ankle.

tidbits.text: Adders lie up in the deep straw, where it's warm. Walk around straw when you can.
Adder venom is half of my antidote. The other half is something I'd rather not name.
Adders were never native to the cellars. Somebody kept them once, in a pit, for reasons of their own.

art.silhouette: coiled snake, head raised

enemies.name: Barrow Ghoul
enemies.text: It was buried once and didn't stay that way. It hits like a coffin lid coming down.

tidbits.text: Barrow ghouls climb out of graves dug too shallow. Barrow and Cairn, the camp's gravediggers, take it personally.
We didn't name them. People hear "barrow" and think of me. I've stopped correcting them.
Ghouls still wear their grave clothes. Some of them still have a coin on each eye.

art.silhouette: hunched grey figure in rags, long arms

enemies.name: Cellar Ooze
enemies.text: Cut it and you have two problems. Hit it hard enough and you have none.

tidbits.text: Oozes grow in the cellar drains, on whatever the old lords washed down there.
An ooze is mostly water and appetite. I've kept one in a jar for a year, and it hasn't forgiven me.
In a dry year an ooze shrinks to a skin on the floor and waits for the wet to come back.

art.silhouette: rounded slime blob, wider at the base

enemies.name: Mimic
enemies.text: Every chest down here is honest. Except this one.

tidbits.text: A mimic copies the chests around it. In a room full of old chests, it's an old chest.
A mimic doesn't eat often. It can sit through a whole winter, waiting for one curious hand.
I check every chest I buy for teeth. Twice. The one time I didn't, I lost a good glove.

art.silhouette: wooden chest, lid open into a mouth

enemies.name: The Rat King
enemies.text: A dozen rats knotted together at the tails under a stolen crown. The crown did this to them.

tidbits.text: The Rat King's crown is the last lord's own. Nobody knows how the rats came by it.
Every rat in the Rat King's knot is cold to the touch, even after it's dead.
We buried a Rat King once. The knot kept moving under the dirt for a week.

enemies.seen_text: Something big sleeps here on a nest of rats, and nothing says you have to wake it.

art.silhouette: bulky rat mass, wider than a normal rat

enemies.name: Sporeling
enemies.text: Stumbling caps of fungus. Kill them at arm's length, or not at all.

art.silhouette: short mushroom creature with stubby legs

enemies.name: Myco Mender
enemies.text: Tends the colony. Kill the gardener and the garden wilts.

art.silhouette: tall thin mushroom figure holding a staff

enemies.name: Shellback
enemies.text: Slow as a cart and twice as heavy. Don't trade blows with it.

tidbits.text: Shellbacks crawl the deep floors and eat whatever comes to rest there. It's why the old halls are so clean.
A shellback's meat is white and sweet. Nobody in town will eat it, knowing what it eats.
Shellbacks shed their shells as they grow. Some of the empty ones down here are big enough to crawl into.

art.silhouette: low beetle with a domed shell

enemies.name: Blind Stalker
enemies.text: No eyes, very good ears. Stand still and it loses you.

art.silhouette: crouched lizard-like hunter, head low

enemies.name: The Bloom Mother
enemies.text: The colony's heart, grown around a warm stone the old lords buried. Every breath it takes, something new sprouts.

art.silhouette: huge bulbous fungus mound filling the tile

items.name: Rusty Dagger
items.text: Short reach, quick hands. You'll land more hits than you'd think.

art.silhouette: short blade with a stubby hilt

items.name: Short Sword
items.text: Garrison steel with the old lords' crest filed off the pommel. Reliable, nothing fancy.

art.silhouette: straight sword

items.name: Hand Axe
items.text: Bites deep when it lands. Doesn't always land.

art.silhouette: short axe, wedge head on a wooden haft

items.name: Spear
items.text: Keeps trouble two steps away, which is the best place for it.

art.silhouette: long thin shaft with a leaf-shaped tip

items.name: Iron Mace
items.text: Not subtle. Bones break, heads ring, skeletons stay down.

art.silhouette: short club with a heavy flanged head

items.name: Shortbow
items.text: Better at a distance. Up close it's an awkward stick.

art.silhouette: curved bow with a nocked arrow

items.name: Ember Wand

charges.recharge: Phase 1: 1 charge per 20 turns. Phase 2: refills at camp.

items.text: Warm to the touch. Five sparks, then it needs a night by the fire.

tidbits.text: Its core is a sliver of deep coal. The people who make them won't say where the coal came from.

art.silhouette: slim wand with a glowing tip

items.name: Traveler's Cloak
items.text: Light enough to dodge in. Stops nothing, but nothing hits you.

art.silhouette: hooded cloak, flared at the hem

items.name: Leather Jerkin
items.text: Scuffed, patched, and still better than your shirt.

art.silhouette: sleeveless tunic shape

items.name: Chain Shirt
items.text: Heavy, loud, and very convincing to anything with teeth.

art.silhouette: short-sleeved shirt shape

items.name: Iron Plate
items.text: You stop dodging. You stop needing to.

art.silhouette: breastplate with broad shoulder plates

items.name: Lantern
items.text: A little more light, a little further. Shows the plates in the floor.

art.silhouette: hanging lantern with a handle loop

items.name: Lucky Knucklebone
items.text: A knucklebone worn smooth by somebody's thumb. Coins seem to find you more often.

art.silhouette: small bone jack with knobbed ends

items.name: Ember Ring
items.text: A coal that never cools, set in brass. Slowly mends you.

art.silhouette: plain ring with a set stone

items.name: Wooden Buckler
items.text: Small, battered, and always in the way of the next hit.

art.silhouette: small heater shield

items.name: Health Potion
items.text: Copper and cloves. Nobody's favorite, but it'll help keep your body in one piece.

tidbits.text: Copper for the blood, cloves for the taste. I've stopped trying to fix the taste.
Every bottle comes out of the alchemist's one cauldron. She won't say what the copper was scraped off.

art.silhouette: round-bellied flask with a narrow neck

items.name: Bandage Roll
items.text: Not fast, but steady. Wrap it and keep walking.

tidbits.text: Cut from shrouds that nobody ended up needing. That's the best kind of shroud to have left over.
A bandage won't close a wound down here. It keeps you walking until something better does.

art.silhouette: rolled cloth with a loose end trailing right

items.name: Stale Bread
items.text: Bread from the bakery in town. It was fresh when it left, which was some time ago.

tidbits.text: People from town still come down for coal. Not all of them go back up, and their bread stays behind.
The bread down here is never more than a few days old. Nobody in town will say who brings it.

art.silhouette: round loaf, wider than tall, top scored twice

items.name: Hard Cheese
items.text: A rind like boot leather. Inside, a small mercy.

tidbits.text: Rats steal cheese from the cellars in town and drag it down here. Even they won't eat it.
Hard cheese keeps a year in the cold. I don't ask how long a wheel has been down there.

art.silhouette: triangular wedge, point to the left

items.name: Antidote Tonic
items.text: Bitter green. Burns going down, burns the poison worse.

tidbits.text: Bring me a live adder and the next tonic's free. Bring me a dead one and we'll talk.

art.silhouette: round-bellied flask, same shape as the health potion

items.name: Smoke Vial
items.text: Break it and vanish for a few breaths. Hitting anything ends it.

tidbits.text: Smoke in a jar. The trick is getting it in there, and I'm not telling you the trick.

art.silhouette: round-bellied flask full of swirling smoke

items.name: Fire Flask
items.text: Throw it, then look away. Everything near the landing catches.

tidbits.text: Lamp oil from the town's last good barrels. Every flask thrown is one less lamp lit up there.
We find what's left after somebody throws one of those indoors. Please don't throw one indoors.

art.silhouette: corked bottle with a burning rag

items.name: Scroll of Mapping
items.text: Ink that crawls into the shape of the floor you're standing on.

tidbits.text: The old lords' surveyors wrote these. The ink still remembers every floor they ever dug.
Now and then the ink draws a room that isn't there. Nobody has gone looking for it.

art.silhouette: parchment with rolled ends top and bottom

items.name: Scroll of Blink
items.text: Read it aloud and you're somewhere else you can see. Mind the landing.

tidbits.text: Every blink scroll is in the same hand. Whoever wrote them wrote thousands, and never signed one.

art.silhouette: parchment with rolled ends top and bottom

items.name: Gold
items.spawn: gold piles per rules.floor_budget; amount per rules.loot.gold_pile
items.text: Shiny, heavy, and worth more at camp than down here.

art.silhouette: single round coin

items.name: Iron Key
items.spawn: Only from the locked_vault room: placed somewhere reachable outside the vault.
items.text: Fits one lock on this floor. Only one.

art.silhouette: old key with a round bow

items.name: Mending Herbs
items.text: Bound green leaves. They only work when someone else applies them.

art.silhouette: small bundle of sprigs

items.name: Whetstone
items.text: One good evening of work at the fire and your blade bites harder.

art.silhouette: slanted gray stone bar

items.name: Ember

use.camp_currency: Goes into the shared pot at camp, spent on upgrades together.

items.text: A deep coal. Banked in a hearth, it stays warm for a lifetime. Most houses are still burning their grandparents' coal.

art.silhouette: small glowing coal

items.name: Torn Page (left half)
items.spawn: Placed by the story system. One player finds the left half, the other the right.
items.text: The left half of a page. The handwriting stops mid-sentence.

art.silhouette: half a page, ragged right edge

items.name: Torn Page (right half)
items.spawn: Placed by the story system. One player finds the left half, the other the right.
items.text: The right half of a page. It starts mid-sentence.

art.silhouette: half a page, ragged left edge

traps.name: Spike Plate
traps.text: A loose flagstone with teeth underneath.

art.silhouette: square floor plate in a frame

traps.name: Snare
traps.text: A noose of old rope. Holds you fast while things arrive.

art.silhouette: rope loop with a stake

traps.name: Alarm Glyph
traps.text: Step on it and everything on the floor hears you.

art.silhouette: rune circle with rays

traps.name: Blink Rune
traps.text: A circle scratched in the stone. It moves you somewhere. Anywhere.

art.silhouette: swirling ring

traps.name: Flame Jet
traps.text: A soot-black nozzle in the wall. You'll smell it first.

art.silhouette: burst of flame streaks

traps.name: Poison Vent
traps.text: A crack in the floor breathing something green.

art.silhouette: floor grate

props.name: Stairs Down
props.use: Ends the floor for you.
props.text: The way down. Whatever's at the bottom is tomorrow's problem.

props.name: Chest
props.use: Open: one item from a rarity roll (per-player loot).
props.text: Latched, not locked. Probably fine.

props.name: Locked Door
props.use: Opens with the iron key, which is used up.
props.text: Iron-banded and very sure of itself.

props.name: Urn
props.use: Bump to break: 30% chance of a gold pile. Breaking makes noise.
props.text: Break it open. Sometimes somebody left a coin inside.

props.name: Bone Pile
props.use: Decor. Also what a reassembling skeleton leaves behind.
props.text: Someone who didn't make it. Maybe someone who isn't finished.

props.name: Healing Spring
props.use: Bump to drink: heal 10. Once per floor.
props.text: Clear water in a stone basin. One good drink.

props.name: Old Shrine
props.use: Bump to pray: lose 4 HP now, gain 'blessed' for the rest of the floor. Once per floor. Asks to confirm.
props.text: A worn altar. It asks for blood and gives back luck.

props.name: Rotted Bookshelf
props.use: Bump to search: may hold a lore page.
props.text: Mostly mold. One page is still legible.

props.name: Cold Fire Ring
props.use: Story site of the pair who came before.
props.text: A cold fire ring and two bedrolls. Someone camped here a long time ago.

props.name: Campfire
props.use: Walk up to rest, cook a meal, or press on (game/deal.js). Only at a stop. (Phase 2's camp screen centerpiece until content 27.)
props.text: A good, steady fire. It's warm, it's bright, and nothing from below will come near it.

props.name: Peddler
props.use: Walk up to sell spare gear and buy supplies (game/deal.js). Only at a stop.
props.text: He buys what you don't need and sells what you will, and he never asks where any of it came from.

tidbits.text: The peddler's stock is whatever comes up the stairs. He has never once said whose it was.
He knows every price in town to the copper, and he hasn't been up to town in years.

props.name: Alchemist
props.use: Walk up to buy rare tonics and scrolls (game/deal.js). Only at a stop.
props.text: She smells of smoke and vinegar, and everything on her table glows a little.

tidbits.text: She goes deeper than you do, alone, and she comes back with jars you aren't allowed to open.
She pays me in tonics. I've never seen her eat, either, now that I think of it.

props.name: The Twins
props.use: Retired in content 28: the twins stand as two props now (twin_elder, twin_younger). Kept so a content 27 stop still loads.
props.text: The pair who carry the stones. Between jobs they stitch up the living. For a fee.

props.name: Barrow
props.use: One of the twins at a stop (intermissions twins): walk up to be patched up, for gold (game/deal.js).
props.text: The elder sister, by four minutes, and the one with the shovel. "Alive. Good. We're behind on stones as it is."

tidbits.text: Barrow has dug more graves than anyone alive. She says she remembers each one, and nobody has caught her out.
She talks to the stones when she thinks I'm asleep. I'm never asleep.

props.name: Cairn
props.use: One of the twins at a stop (intermissions twins): walk up to be patched up, for gold (game/deal.js).
props.text: The younger sister. She holds the lantern while Barrow digs, carves the stones, and sews the neater seam, for a fee.

tidbits.text: Cairn carves every stone by lantern light. She won't carve a name until someone tells her how it's spelled.
Her stitches are neater than mine. Mine hold longer. We don't talk about it.

props.name: Small Table
props.use: Furniture (content 29): the twins' table at a stop, in the way; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: The sisters' table: two cups, one candle, and a deck of cards nobody else gets dealt into.

props.name: Shut Gate
props.use: Furniture (content 31): across a camp guest's spoke while they're away; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: Shut and latched. Whoever keeps this room is out on the stairs tonight.

props.name: Clay Pot
props.use: Bump to break (content 32, the camp): 20% chance of 1-3 gold.
props.text: Somebody's spare crockery. Breaking it seems to be a camp tradition.

props.name: Old Barrel
props.use: Bump to break (content 32, the camp): 20% chance of 1-3 gold.
props.text: An old barrel. There may be something left in the bottom.

props.name: Log Seat
props.use: Furniture (content 33): a seat round the camp's fire, in the way; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: A log worn smooth on top. Whoever sat here last left the warm end for you.

props.name: Trade Table
props.use: Furniture (content 35): the peddler's counter at a stop, in the way; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: Scuffed oak, brass scales, and a ledger the peddler slams shut whenever you lean in.

props.name: Camp Chair
props.use: Furniture (content 35): the peddler's chair at a stop, in the way; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: A folding chair, more patches than canvas. The peddler never sits in it, and nobody else may.

props.name: Stump Stool
props.use: Furniture (content 33): a seat round the camp's fire, in the way; a bump shows its line and takes no turn.
props.text: A sawn stump with a dip worn in the middle. Initials carved in the side, half scratched out.

cover.name: Shallow Water
cover.text: Cold, ankle-deep, and very good at putting things out.

cover.name: Straw
cover.text: Old bedding, dry as paper. Something sleeps on it, or did.

cover.name: Scorched Floor
cover.text: Black stone and a smell of smoke. Whatever was here is gone.

dressing.name: Flagstones
dressing.text: Big square stones, laid by someone who cared.

dressing.name: Wood Planks
dressing.text: Old boards. They tell everyone where you are.

dressing.name: Cracked Stone
dressing.text: The floor gave up here, a little.

dressing.name: Mossy Stone
dressing.text: Damp enough for moss. Not much else likes it.

dressing.name: Mossy Wall
dressing.text: Green creeps down from the ceiling.

dressing.name: Cracked Brick
dressing.text: Bricks split by roots, or by time.

dressing.name: Cracked Brick
dressing.text: A split runs down from the ceiling. It's been running for years.

dressing.name: Cracked Brick
dressing.text: The bottom course is giving way. Nobody's coming to fix it.

dressing.name: Tapestry
dressing.text: A hunting scene, mostly moth holes now.

dressing.name: Painting
dressing.text: A stern portrait of someone important. The nameplate has been pried off.

dressing.name: Banner
dressing.text: The old lords' colors, with their crest cut out. Someone went to a lot of trouble to forget them.

dressing.name: Floor Grate
dressing.text: Iron bars over a drain. Something drips down there.

dressing.name: Rubble
dressing.text: A bit of the ceiling, come down to visit.

dressing.name: Woven Rug
dressing.text: Threadbare, but somebody wove it with care.

dressing.name: Diamond Rug
dressing.text: Diamonds on diamonds, faded to the weft.

room_themes.name: Plain
room_themes.text: Bare stone, like most of the cellars.

room_themes.name: Storeroom
room_themes.text: Boards underfoot, and whatever was stored here is long gone.

room_themes.name: Hall
room_themes.text: Flagstones and old hangings. Someone held court here.

room_themes.name: Study
room_themes.text: A rug, a painting, a chair on its side.

room_themes.name: Cistern
room_themes.text: Damp stone and drains. The water went somewhere.

intermissions.known_text: "You again. We kept the shovel by the door." Between burials, the sisters patch up the living.

light_sources.name: Wall Torch
light_sources.text: Someone keeps these torches lit, even this far down. Nobody at camp knows who.

rooms.name: Locked Vault
rooms.contains: locked_door, a chest rolled at uncommon or better, one gold pile. The iron_key spawns elsewhere, always reachable without going through the vault.
rooms.text: A barred door, a lock, and somewhere on this floor a key.

rooms.name: Shrine
rooms.text: A worn altar. It asks for blood and gives back luck.

rooms.name: Spring
rooms.text: Clear water in a stone basin. One good drink.

rooms.name: Den
rooms.contains: A group of 3-4 biome enemies, all asleep, plus 2 gold piles and a chest.
rooms.text: A nest of sleepers and the things they've hoarded.

rooms.name: Trapped Hall
rooms.contains: A corridor at least 6 tiles long with 2-3 traps and a chest at the far end.
rooms.text: A long hall, a chest at the end, and a floor that doesn't look right.

rooms.name: Lore Nook
rooms.text: A shelf of rotted books. One page is still legible.

rooms.name: Cold Camp
rooms.contains: cold_fire_ring and story items. Placed by the story system on chosen floors, never rolled randomly.

omens.name: Still Air
omens.text: The air is still. Just you and the dark.

omens.name: Long Night
omens.text: The torches are burning low. Everyone sees less, monsters included.

omens.name: Restless
omens.text: Something has stirred the deep, and more of them are about tonight.

omens.name: Hushed
omens.text: The whole floor is sleeping. Tread softly.

omens.name: Brittle Stone
omens.text: The floor is riddled with old traps, but they're easier to spot.

omens.name: Echoing
omens.text: You can hear your partner's footsteps from the start.

omens.name: Ember Tide
omens.text: Deep coals rise to the surface.

cellar_rat: Pulled down by rats. There wasn't much left to bury.
Killed by rats, one bite at a time. It took most of an afternoon.
The rats came out of the walls, the drains and the straw, and kept coming.
Any one of those rats on its own would have been nothing.
The torch went out while they were fighting rats. After that, the rats had the best of it.
Overrun by rats in a storeroom full of empty barrels.
Killed by rats in the cellars.
Killed by rats in the old lords' larder. There was nothing else left in it to eat.
We had to chase the rats off before we could start digging.
So many bites that nobody could say which one did it.
Cornered by rats against a wall of barrels.
They killed eleven rats. The twelfth was the problem.
Killed by rats on the way to the stairs.
One rat is nothing. Forty rats killed them.
The rats left the boots. Rats always leave the boots.
cave_bat: Killed by a bat they never managed to hit.
They swung at the bat a dozen times. It was somewhere else every time.
A bat bit them on the neck while they were busy with something else.
Killed by bats in the dark.
The bat flew like a dropped leaf, and every swing went where it had just been.
They died with their sword up, waiting for the bat to come back. It did.
We found them in a cave full of wingbeats. We didn't stay long.
Bitten by bats until they couldn't stand.
It's hard to fight something you can only hear.
They chased a bat into the next room. More bats lived there.
Killed by a bat no bigger than their hand.
Lost to bats in a cave too dark to see the ceiling.
The last thing they heard was wings.
Every time they turned, the bat was behind them.
skeleton: Killed by a skeleton that had already died once. It got back up. They didn't.
They knocked the skeleton down three times. It got up four.
Killed by a skeleton still wearing an old work belt. It had been dead a very long time.
They didn't break the bones while they had the chance.
Killed by bones that wouldn't stay in a heap.
The skeleton was slow, but it was patient, and it never got tired.
Killed by something that should have stayed buried. We dug this one deep.
Struck down by the dead in the old workings.
Killed by a skeleton near the old shafts.
The bones put themselves back together while they were catching their breath.
The skeleton had a pick handle, and it still knew how to swing it.
They turned their back on a pile of bones. The pile stood up.
Beaten by the dead, who don't get tired and don't give up.
Their bones are here now. We made sure they'll stay put.
goblin_cutpurse: Robbed and stabbed by a goblin, in that order.
The goblin took their purse, then came back for the rest.
They chased a goblin around a corner. Three more goblins were waiting.
Stabbed by a goblin over a handful of coins.
Killed by a goblin cutpurse, who ran off with their gold.
They died holding on to their purse. The goblin got it anyway.
The goblin had a knife up its sleeve and another in its boot.
Robbed in the torchlight by something half their height.
The goblins keep a tally of everyone they rob, scratched into a wall. They're on it now.
The goblin wanted their boots as well. We buried them barefoot.
They followed a goblin into the dark to get their gold back.
Stabbed in the back by a thief while they were watching the front.
The goblin cut their purse strings first and their throat second.
Killed by a cutpurse. Their pockets were turned out by the time we got there.
web_spinner: Caught in a web and bled slowly. The spider was in no hurry.
They walked into a web in the dark and couldn't pull free.
Wrapped in silk and left hanging for later.
The spider came down from the ceiling while they were watching the floor.
Killed by a web spinner in a dark corridor.
The more they struggled, the tighter the web held.
We had to cut them down before we could bury them.
Held in the web long enough for the spider to take its time.
Bitten by a spider while they were stuck fast in its web.
The web crossed the doorway at head height. They never saw it.
Eight legs, and every one of them faster than theirs.
Wrapped up like a parcel and hung in a corner.
Stuck in a web, watching the spider come down the thread.
The silk is still in their hair. We couldn't get all of it out.
cellar_ooze: Every cut made more of it. In the end there was too much.
They cut the ooze in half, and then there were two.
Dissolved by an ooze in a flooded cellar.
They kept swinging, and the ooze kept splitting.
Smothered by ooze on a cellar floor.
By the end, the ooze covered the floor from wall to wall.
The ooze had taken most of them by the time we came. We buried the boots.
Swallowed by something with no mouth.
The ooze grew every time it was hit, and they hit it a great many times.
Cornered by a crowd of oozes, every one of them from the same ooze.
Eaten by an ooze they took for a wet patch on the floor.
They fought the ooze until their arms gave out.
Too many oozes and not enough room to run.
Every piece of the ooze still wanted them.
chest_mimic: Opened the chest. The chest opened back.
Bitten by a chest they were trying to open.
They reached into the chest, and the chest closed on their arm.
The chest had teeth under the lid.
Eaten by a chest in a room with nothing else in it.
Killed by a mimic made up to look like a chest.
The lid came down like a jaw, because it was one.
They came down here for treasure. The treasure was hungry.
We had to pry the chest open to get them out.
The latch was its tongue. They found out when they touched it.
They kicked every other chest on the floor first. Not this one.
Killed by the one chest they didn't check.
They had their hands on the gold when the lid came down.
Swallowed by a chest. Their gold is still inside it.
rat_king: Killed by the Rat King, who wears a crown that isn't his.
They fought the Rat King in its own hall and lost.
A dozen rats knotted together, and all of them biting at once.
The Rat King called, and its court came out of the walls.
Killed by the Rat King on floor {floor}.
They reached for the crown. Every rat in the hall saw them do it.
The crown is cold, they say. They never got close enough to find out.
Brought down by the Rat King and a hundred of its subjects.
We waited until the rats went quiet before we went in for them.
The Rat King never fights alone. Nothing that wears a crown does.
Bowed to no rat, and died in the Rat King's hall.
The knot of rats pulled them down like a single animal.
spike_plate: Stepped on the wrong flagstone. It was full of spikes.
The spikes came up through the floor and through their boots.
Killed by a spike trap set long before they were born.
Killed by a trap in the floor of a quiet corridor.
They watched the walls. The floor was the problem.
The trap was older than the town, and it still worked.
We had to push the spikes back down to get them out.
They stepped on the one stone everyone else had stepped around.
The old lords built their traps to last.
Killed by spikes in the floor, a long way from help.
The flagstone clicked. They had just enough time to hear it.
snare: Caught by the ankle in a snare. Something came to see what it had caught.
Snared by the ankle and held there until the monsters came.
Held fast by an old snare while the whole floor came to look.
flame_jet: The wall breathed fire as they walked past it.
Burned by a jet of fire from a crack in the wall.
They saw the scorch marks on the floor and walked over them anyway.
A gout of flame from the stonework, and no water anywhere near.
Killed by a fire trap the old lords left behind.
The jet fired once. Once was plenty.
They stood in front of the vent a moment too long.
We found them by the scorch marks on the wall.
The flame came out of the wall at waist height.
Burned in a corridor where the walls were already black.
shrine: The shrine asked for blood. They gave it all of it.
They knelt at the shrine and didn't get up.
Prayed for strength and paid for it with the last of their blood.
The shrine took what it was owed, and then a little more.
Bled out at an old shrine. Nobody knows who it was built for.
They asked something old for help. It took its price first.
We found them still kneeling at the shrine.
Faith is expensive this far down.
fire_flask: Threw a fire flask and walked straight into the fire.
A good throw. They were standing too close to where it landed.
Burned by their own fire flask.
The flask broke right where they aimed it. Then they walked in after it.
They set the room alight to save themselves. It didn't.
Caught in their own fire with nowhere to step back to.
The fire spread faster than they could walk.
We put out what was left of the fire with sand, and then we buried them.
They threw the flask at a rat and set the whole room on fire.
poisoned: The poison took its time, and it finished the job.
Every breath stung, and then there weren't any more.
Poisoned, and too far from anyone with an antidote.
They felt fine for a while. Then they didn't.
The bite was small. The poison wasn't.
They breathed the bad air one breath too long.
Their lips had gone blue by the time we found them.
They kept walking with the poison in them, looking for the stairs.
The venom worked slowly and never stopped.
Poisoned and alone, three rooms from the stairs.
burning: Burned in the straw. We buried what the fire left.
Caught fire and couldn't put it out.
They ran while they were burning, which only made it worse.
Burned to death a long way from any water.
The fire caught their cloak first, then everything else.
They found the water one turn too late.
Their armor was still warm when we got to them.
They burned for a long time, and nobody came.
They rolled on the floor, which doesn't help when the floor is straw.
The flames were on their back before they knew it.
Burned in a corridor full of old straw.
fire: Lit the straw and stood too close to it.
The straw went up, and so did they.
The fire spread across the straw faster than they could run.
Killed by a fire that started in the straw.
They watched the fire spread from the wrong side of it.
The whole room burned, and they were in it.
We waited for the stones to cool before we went in.
The fire came across the floor like water.
The smoke got them before the fire did.
Fire spreads, and they didn't move fast enough.

context.line: Died with {count} potions unopened. We'll see they aren't wasted.
Saved {count} health potions for later. There wasn't a later.
{count} health potions in the pack, and every one of them still corked.
They died thirsty with {count} potions on their belt.
Died within three steps of the stairs. We measured.
They could see the stairs from where they fell.
The stairs were right there. They could see the top step.
A few more steps and they'd have been done with floor {floor}.
Died carrying {gold} gold. It didn't help.
{gold} gold in the pack, and nothing down here to spend it on.
We counted {gold} gold on them. We left it where it was.
The richest person on floor {floor}, for a little while.
Killed on turn {turn}, before their eyes had adjusted to the dark.
It was only turn {turn}. They had barely started.
Their boots were still clean on turn {turn}.
They lasted until turn {turn}. It was a short visit.
They saw every corner of floor {floor}. Something was waiting in the last one.
They mapped the whole floor and died in the last room.
They went everywhere on this floor. That's how it found them.
Buried in iron plate. It took both of us to lift.
The iron plate held. The rest of them didn't.
Their iron plate stopped everything except the last one.
Hidden from everything except the thing that killed them.
They died where nobody could see them. We nearly didn't find them.
They were hiding in the dark. Something else was hiding better.
They'd come through a great deal down here. Then a rat.
Killed by a rat, after everything else they'd lived through.
They'd killed far worse than rats. It was a rat that did it.
Died on the first floor. They didn't get far.
Killed on floor one, close enough to the town to smell the bread.
Some people never get past the first floor. They were one of them.
We dig more graves for floor one than for anywhere else.
They stepped on the alarm glyph, and everything on the floor came running.
The alarm went off, and they were still standing on it when the first ones came.
The alarm woke the whole floor, and the whole floor was hungry.
The rune moved them somewhere worse.
They blinked out of danger and into a room full of it.
Teleported into the middle of something that was already awake.
Died of poison with an antidote in the pack.
The cure was in their pocket the whole time.
We found the antidote when we emptied their pack. It was still sealed.
Carried everything and used none of it.
Their pack was full of things that might have helped.
They were saving it all for a worse day. There wasn't one.
Stone number {attempt} on this floor. We'd only just finished the last one.
Back on this floor for try {attempt}. It ended the same way.
They came back to this floor, and so did the monsters.
This floor has killed them more than once now.
We've started keeping their stones in a row.
They knew this floor by heart by the end. It didn't save them.
That was try {attempt}. They'd learned a lot, but not quite enough.
Another try on this floor, and another stone.
The floor remembered them, and so did everything on it.
They've tried this floor {attempt} times. We've stopped being surprised.
Their old sack was right there, close enough to touch.
Died reaching for their own sack.
One more step and they'd have had their things back.
They fell beside the sack they lost the last time.
Their old sack and their new stone, side by side.
We found them with one hand on the sack.

generic: Killed by the {killer}, a long way from home.
The {killer} got the last word.
They saw the {killer} too late to run.
They were sure they could handle one {killer}.
They had the {killer} nearly beaten.
They turned their back on the {killer} for one moment.
The {killer} came out of the dark, and that was that.
Met the {killer} in a narrow corridor with nowhere to go.
The last thing they saw was the {killer}, much too close.
The {killer} walked away from it. They didn't.
We know the {killer}'s work when we see it.
They underestimated the {killer}, once.
They fought the {killer} to the last, and the {killer} is still out there.
Killed by the {killer} with the stairs nowhere in sight.
They tried to talk their way past the {killer}. It wasn't listening.
Went down the stairs and never came back up.
Their footsteps stop here.
Not the first to fall down here, and not the last.
They died in the dark, a long way from the stairs.
They went further down than most people do.
Died alone on floor {floor}.
They were brave, and it wasn't enough.
Gone, with the torch still burning in its bracket beside them.
Somebody's child, a long way underground.
Died on turn {turn}. Cairn carved the number neatly.
Their pack outlived them.
Most people don't come back up. Neither did they.
They fought until they couldn't.
Down here, everyone gets a stone eventually.
They wanted to see what was further down.
Lost in the dark under the ruin.
The torches burned all night beside them.
We dug this one deep, to be sure.
We didn't know them well. We buried them carefully anyway.
We brought them up the stairs on an old door.
We cleaned their face before we closed the lid.
We had a stone ready. We always do.
We'll keep a candle lit on this one for a while.
We spelled their name right. We checked twice.
Barrow dug the hole. Cairn did the lettering.
They had a plan. It had a hole in it.
They lit a torch to see better. Everything else saw them too.
They waited one turn too long.
One more room, they said.
They ran, but not fast enough.
They didn't run, and should have.
Brave enough to go first, unlucky enough to stay.
They packed a lunch. It was still in the pack.
Died doing what they loved, which was going one room further.
Their courage lasted longer than they did.
They fought well, and they fought alone.
Fearless, which turned out to be the problem.
They went looking for trouble and found it in the first room.
They stood their ground, and the ground kept them.
The death was quick. The walk down here took longer.
They went back for a dropped coin.
If found, please return to the surface.
Somewhere, a bard is making this sound braver than it was.
They used their last potion on the second-to-last fight.
They saw the danger and walked toward it.
Their last turn was their worst one.
A short career, and an honest one.
Their shield was split clean down the middle.
They'd been doing so well.
They checked every chest for traps and forgot about the floor.
We closed their eyes. They looked surprised.
They tripped on a loose flagstone at the worst moment.
They went down swinging, and mostly missing.
They took a wrong turn somewhere on floor {floor}.
Died on floor {floor} with their boots on.
The floor was quiet right up until it wasn't.
They walked into an unlit room without a torch.
They heard something behind them and didn't look.
They were sure the room was empty.
May the next one learn from this one.
They kept going after they should have stopped.
A good fighter on a bad day.
They died with their back to a wall and nowhere else to go.
Rest now. We'll keep the rats off.

lead: Your sack is where you fell, with {loot}.
You dropped {loot} when you went down.
Your sack is still down there with {loot}.
A sack where you fell holds {loot}.
You left {loot} where you died.
Your sack fell with you. It has {loot}.
Your sack still has {loot} in it.
The sack you dropped holds {loot}.
The rats haven't found {loot} yet.
Your sack is waiting where you fell: {loot}.
It's all still in your sack: {loot}.
Everything you found is in your sack: {loot}.
Your sack hit the floor with {loot}.
You went down holding {loot}.
Where you fell, a sack holds {loot}.
Your sack is lying where you fell: {loot}.
Your sack lies in the dark with {loot}.
You'll find {loot} where you fell.
A sack lies where you died, with {loot}.
What you carried is where you fell: {loot}.
Your sack is still there with {loot}.
You can still get back {loot}.
You let go of {loot} when you fell.
Your sack holds {loot}.
Down where you fell, your sack holds {loot}.
close: Go and get it back.
Die again first, and it's gone.
Whatever killed you is still near it.
Get there before the rats do.
You know the way now.
It's yours if you can reach it.
Pick it up on your way to the stairs.
It's one trip. Make it a careful one.
Reach it before you fall again.
Take it back.
Fetch it, and go slower this time.
It's still yours, for now.
Get it back without leaving another.
It's a short walk if you're careful.
What got you may be standing over it.
You only get one more chance at it.
The floor won't hold it for you twice.
Nothing down there will keep it safe.
Go now, while it's still there.
Get it, then get out.
The rats will find it if you don't.
Mind whatever put you down.
Bring it back with you this time.
It's the same floor. Go and get it.
Fall again before then, and it's lost.

no_sack: You had nothing on you, so there's nothing to go back for.
You found nothing on this floor, so you lost nothing.
Your pockets were empty when you fell. Nothing is waiting for you.
There's no sack this time. You hadn't picked anything up.
You died empty-handed, so there's nothing to fetch.
Nothing of yours is lying down there. Just go.
All you lost was the time it took.
You hadn't found a single coin yet, so there's nothing to recover.
You had nothing worth carrying, so there is nothing to carry back.
There's nothing to recover. Start again, and go carefully.
There's no sack, because you had nothing to put in one.
You lost nothing but the walk. Walk it again.
The floor gave you nothing, and it kept nothing of yours.
Your hands were empty when you fell, and they still are.
The rats will be disappointed. You left them nothing.
Nothing fell with you. You can head straight for the stairs.
Nothing was lost except the ground you'd covered.
You were traveling light, so nothing is waiting where you fell.
You hadn't found anything yet, so nothing is lost.
Nobody has to carry anything back. There's nothing there.
There's nothing on the floor with your name on it.
You fell with empty hands. At least nothing else was lost.
No gold, no gear and no sack. It's just the floor again.
You'd picked up nothing, so the floor has nothing to keep.
There's nothing to go back for, only the way down.
The only thing waiting where you fell is whatever killed you.
You owe the floor nothing, and it owes you nothing.
There's nothing in your hands and nothing in a sack. Go again.
There's nothing to save from this one.
Your pockets stayed light. That's the one good thing about it.
You left nothing behind except a scuff where you fell.
lost_sack: Your old sack is gone. The rats got to it first.
Your last sack is gone for good.
You fell again before you reached your old sack, so it's gone.
The rats dragged your old sack off while you were away.
Your first sack is lost, and nobody is bringing it back.
The sack from your last try is gone, with everything in it.
Something down there took your old sack. It isn't giving it back.
Your old sack is a rat's nest now.
The goblins found your old sack. They won't be returning it.
Your old sack has been picked clean.
Your old sack is gone. All that's left is the spot where it was.

omen_rules: One omen per floor, rolled from the shared floor seed so both players get the same one. Guardian floors never roll an omen. Show the omen's text when the floor starts and in the message log. Effect keys: sight_mod_all (added to everyone's sight, minimum 2), light_mod_all (added to every light's radius, the player's included, minimum 1), extra_monsters, extra_traps, extra_items (added to the floor budget), xp_mult, gold_mult, ember_mult (multipliers), monsters_start (overrides every monster's start state), detect_mod (added to trap detection), ghost_full_path (show the partner's whole route from the start).
